strategy.summary: Reproduce numba/numba#10088: incorrect special-value handling (NaN) in the np.unique/np.union1d overload used by @njit, causing union1d to return an extra 1.0 element alongside NaN instead of only [nan]. Build a targeted test that compares jitted output to non-jitted output via np.testing.assert_equal, with a NaN-containing input that triggers the tail/deduplication logic.

pinned_because: numpy 2.1.3 (explicit and numerically relevant; provided by issue#10069 environment)
numba 0.61.0 (explicit and numerically relevant; provided by issue#10069 environment)

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (commit 934a8e4426ff on top of the pinned environment: Python 3.10.16, numpy 2.1.3, numba 0.61.0 build), the test `test_union1d_nan_dedup_matches_python` fails with an assertion mismatch because the jitted result includes an extra element (e.g. actual `array([ 1., nan])` with shape (2,) instead of expected `array([nan])` with shape (1,)). On the fixed revision for PR #10088, the same test passes because the NaN-aware deduplication change propagates to the np.union1d overload so the jitted output matches the non-jitted output (expected only `array([nan])`).
strategy.numerical_probe: Using NaN special-value comparisons indirectly through union1d/unique dedup logic under @njit; the probe is whether NaNs are treated as equal for uniqueness/deduplication so union1d does not incorrectly retain extra distinct tail values.
risks: This bug is specific to the njit compilation path that uses numba’s overloads for np.unique/np.union1d; if the test does not run under @njit, the mismatch may not appear.
The behavior is tied to NaN handling; if inputs don’t contain np.nan (including the 'nan,nan' case), the NaN-aware deduplication logic may not trigger.
If reproduction is done on a different numpy version than 2.1.3, the overload behavior and/or reference outputs may differ, so the test might not transition.

If the fixed commit is not actually incorporated (i.e., you build without the PR’s change), the buggy behavior will persist and the test will keep failing; ensure you build/test both buggy and fixed revisions.

Potential architecture/toolchain sensitivity: if your LLVM/backend differs materially, edge-case codegen differences could affect whether the incorrect element appears; if that happens, run on the same platform/CI image used to validate #10088.

oracle.reference_source: numpy reference (non-jitted) behavior for np.union1d/np.unique under the same numpy==2.1.3
oracle.why: The test relies on np.testing.assert_equal comparing shapes and values exactly, and the mismatch is described as a wrong shape/value inclusion (e.g. (2,) vs (1,) and presence of 1.0 alongside nan).

strategy.fails_on_buggy: Assertion sees a shape/value mismatch: jitted `np.union1d([nan],[nan])` returns an array containing both `1.0` and `nan` (e.g. `array([ 1., nan])`, shape (2,)), while the non-jitted `np.union1d([nan],[nan])` returns only `array([nan])` (shape (1,)).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: jitted `np.union1d([nan],[nan])` matches the non-jitted result exactly: `array([nan])` only (shape (1,)), because the NaN-aware deduplication fix in the np.unique overload propagates to the np.union1d overload.
